units.216.858 apuntes contables de tres empres: 216,858 journal entries from three companies in a Power BI model that joins the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow, with drill-through down to the source entry.
units.Cómo convertí 216.858 apuntes contables: How I turned 216,858 journal entries from three companies into a Power BI model that connects the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow. Free cash flow went from −€1.17m to €678,209 in one year — the model shows exactly which items explain the difference.
units.Balance, PyG y Cash Flow conectados en u: Balance sheet, P&L and cash flow connected in a single model, with drill-through down to the journal entry. Free cash flow 2023: €678,209 (from −€1,165,650 the year before).
units.Cómo convertí 216.858 apuntes contables: How I turned 216,858 journal entries into a financial report anyone can explore
Three companies. Two years of accounts. A single model that connects the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow without leaving Power BI.
units.Si nunca has trabajado con contabilidad,: If you’ve never worked with accounting, think of it as three different questions about the same company.
units.¿Qué tiene y qué debe la empresa hoy?: What does the company own and owe today?
units.Aquí aparecen activos como la tesorería: This is where assets such as cash or stock appear, along with debts and equity.
units.¿Cómo ha ganado o perdido dinero durante: How has it made or lost money during the year?
units.Aquí aparecen ingresos, gastos, EBITDA y: This is where revenue, expenses, EBITDA and profit appear.
units.¿Ha entrado o salido dinero de la caja?: Has money come into or gone out of the till?
units.Porque una empresa puede tener beneficio: Because a company can make a profit and still run out of cash.
units.El reto es que estas tres piezas debería: The challenge is that these three pieces should tell the same story. And that’s exactly what I tried to build.
units.Cuando cada empresa cuenta una historia: When each company tells a different story.
units.Los datos ya existían. Había tres empres: The data already existed. There were three different companies, each with its own journal, and together they had built up 216,858 entries across 2022 and 2023.
units.El problema aparecía cuando querías resp: The problem came when you wanted to answer something as simple as:
units.¿Cómo está realmente el grupo?: How is the group really doing?
units.Balance, PyG y Cash Flow podían consulta: The balance sheet, P&L and cash flow could be viewed separately, but there was no consolidated view that let you move between them without rebuilding the analysis by hand.
units.Cuantas más versiones del mismo informe: The more versions of the same report there are, the easier it is for two people to reach different conclusions from supposedly identical data. My aim was to prevent exactly that.
units.La idea que cambió el proyecto: The idea that changed the project
units.Quería que cualquier KPI pudiera defende: I wanted every KPI to be able to stand on its own.
units.Mientras diseñaba el modelo me hice una: While designing the model, I asked myself a question.
units.¿Qué pasa si alguien me pregunta de dónd: What happens if someone asks me where this number comes from?
I didn’t want to answer by opening Excel.
I wanted to answer with a click.
units.Por eso todo el informe gira alrededor d: That’s why the whole report revolves around a very simple idea.
units.Cada cifra debería poder recorrerse hast: Every figure should be traceable down to the entry that created it.
units.Ese principio acabó condicionando prácti: That principle ended up shaping almost every decision in the project.
units.Hoy ese recorrido existe de verdad: desd: Today that path really exists: from the trial balance — €187,730,234.71 of debits matching exactly €187,730,234.71 of credits — I can drill down to a sub-account, from there to its general ledger, and from there to a specific entry. Without leaving the report.
units.Empecé por el modelo, no por los gráfico: I started with the model, not the charts.
units.Muchos dashboards empiezan diseñando vis: Many dashboards start by designing visuals.
units.Primero construí un modelo capaz de sopo: First I built a model able to support three different financial statements without duplicating logic or breaking calculations.
units.En el centro están <strong>FactDiario</s: At the centre are FactDiario, with the actual journal entries, and FactPresupuesto, with the budget data. Both connect to the same nine dimensions: Calendar, Companies, Sources, Accounts, Partners, and the four that give shape to each financial statement — dimPyG, dimBalance, dimCF and DimApuntes.
units.La única relación bidireccional del mode: The model’s only bidirectional relationship connects FactDiario with DimApuntes. I left it that way because it was needed to calculate cash flow correctly when filtering by entry type. Everything else keeps a single filter direction, so the model behaves more predictably.
units.Una decisión que me ahorró muchos proble: A decision that saved me a lot of trouble
units.Durante el desarrollo descubrí que inten: During the build I found that trying to mix both scenarios in a single table made the calculations much more complicated. Separating them meant any comparison worked exactly the same way throughout the report.
units.FactDiario y FactPresupuesto comparten l: FactDiario and FactPresupuesto share the same dimensions, so the budget variance reuses the same filter context as any other measure — and so does the year-end projection. No duplicated logic anywhere in the model.
units.Esta separación es la que permite compar: This separation is what makes it possible to compare actual vs budget at any level, from the group total down to a single company, without breaking consistency between the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow.
units.El pequeño detalle que hace que el infor: The small detail that makes the report more reliable
units.Hay una página que normalmente pasa desa: There’s one page that usually goes unnoticed.
And yet it’s one of my favourites.
units.Antes de analizar resultados, el modelo: Before analysing results, the model automatically checks whether there are:
units.La tabla <strong>Cuentas sin clasificar<: The Unclassified accounts table is recalculated on every refresh. That means the report itself tries to catch errors before they show up as if they were real results.
units.Me parecía más útil construir esa protec: It seemed more useful to build that safeguard into the model than to rely on manual reviews afterwards.
units.Con los tres años de datos cargados, hoy: With the three years of data loaded, the checklist now comes out clean: zero unbalanced entries, zero unclassified accounts. It’s the first screen I look at before trusting any figure in the rest of the report.
units.Proyectar un cierre sin inventarme los d: Projecting a year end without inventing the data.
units.Probablemente la medida que más tiempo m: The measure that took me longest was probably the year-end projection.
Up to October I use actual data.
From there on, I use the budget.
units.Pero hacerlo sin romper gráficos ni tabl: But doing it without breaking charts or tables was far more complicated. There’s a configurable cut-off date in the model — set to 31 October 2023 — after which every measure automatically switches from actual data to budget, and the chart series stays visually continuous instead of leaving a gap between actual and projected.
units.El resultado, mes a mes: <strong>309.284: The result, month by month: €309,284.99 of actuals accumulated up to the cut-off, against the €173,511.68 the original budget expected for the whole year. The combined year-end projection comes to €196,404.62 — neither the actual nor the budgeted figure, but the best estimate with the information available at each point.
units.Ese fue probablemente el momento en el q: That was probably when I learnt the most about DAX during this project.
units.Trece páginas de contenido. Siete que so: Thirteen content pages. Seven that only appear when you need them.
units.El informe tiene 20 páginas en total. Se: The report has 20 pages in total. You navigate from a fixed header with five entry points — Home · Checklist · Trial balance · Balance sheet · P&L · Cash flow — but each block hides its own path into the detail.
units.Cada bloque responde a una pregunta dist: Each block answers a different question.
units.<strong>Inicio</strong> → un panel con 1: Home → a panel with 12 KPIs that sums up the situation in seconds.
units.<strong>Checklist</strong> → ¿puedo conf: Checklist → can I trust the data before analysing it?
units.<strong>Balance de sumas y saldos</stron: Trial balance → its own three-page block: from the aggregated account to the individual entry (Trial balance → General ledger → Entry detail).
units.<strong>Balance</strong> → estructura pa: Balance sheet → financial structure and how it evolves, with a second page for the month-by-month detail.
units.<strong>PyG</strong> → cuatro vistas: ev: P&L → four views: quarterly trend, year-on-year comparison, variance against budget and year-end projection.
units.<strong>Cash Flow</strong> → de dónde vi: Cash flow → where the group’s cash comes from and where it goes.
units.Las 7 páginas restantes no aparecen en n: The other 7 pages don’t appear in any menu: they’re tooltip pages, which Power BI shows floating when I hover over a point on the balance sheet, P&L or treasury trend charts. Instead of the basic tooltip, a mini-page appears with the figure properly formatted and the same visual identity as the rest of the report. Most reports use one or two pages like this; I used seven, one for each chart that needed it.

units.El dato que mejor resume el proyecto: The figure that best sums up the project
units.La caja cambió por completo de un año pa: Cash changed completely from one year to the next.
units.Lo importante no era quedarse con la cif: What mattered wasn’t the figure itself. What mattered was being able to explain which items made up that result without redoing the analysis from scratch.
units.Ese cambio fue el momento en el que sent: That change was the moment I felt the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow stopped being three separate reports and became a single story.
units.Modelo completo, la navegación entre las: The complete model, navigation across the report’s 20 pages (13 content pages, 7 tooltip pages) and drill-through from any KPI down to the source journal entry.
units.Ratios de solvencia y liquidez, cálculos: Solvency and liquidity ratios, EBITDA calculations, year-on-year change, variance against budget and the year-end projection logic.
units.19 tablas y 15 relaciones: FactDiario y: 19 tables and 15 relationships: FactDiario and FactPresupuesto connected to nine shared and hierarchy dimensions.
units.Navegación desde cualquier KPI de alto n: Navigation from any high-level KPI down to the individual journal entry that creates it.
units.Detecta asientos descuadrados y cuentas: Catches unbalanced entries and unclassified accounts before they reach the analysis.
units.Extrapola el resultado esperado a fin de: Extrapolates the expected result at year end, combining actual data up to the cut-off date.
units.El mejor dashboard empieza mucho antes d: The best dashboard starts long before the dashboard.
units.Si tuviera que resumir el aprendizaje de: If I had to sum up what I learnt from this project, I wouldn’t talk about the 174 DAX measures.
units.Aprendí que un buen dashboard no depende: I learnt that a good dashboard doesn’t depend only on visual design.
units.Depende de que cada cifra tenga sentido,: It depends on every figure making sense, being checkable and staying consistent when you change company, period or financial statement.
units.Ese cambio de mentalidad es probablement: That change of mindset is probably the most valuable thing I take away from this project.
units.De miles de movimientos contables a una: From thousands of accounting movements to a single financial story.
units.Este proyecto me permitió unir varias co: This project let me bring together several things I’m particularly interested in: data modelling, DAX, visualisation and business analysis.
units.El resultado es un informe que intenta h: The result is a report that tries to do something very simple to say and much harder to build.
units.Que cualquier cifra pueda explicarse sin: Any figure can be explained without leaving the dashboard.
